slop-cop runs regex + structural detectors (and optional Codex-backed semantic analysis) over a piece of text, and prints a JSON report aimed at other agents. Input is read from the file argument or from stdin when the argument is "-" or omitted. Output is JSON on stdout; errors go to stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, including a run that found violations 1 check --strict completed and the report carries violations 2 input/IO error 3 LLM subprocess error 4 flag/usage error Usage: slop-cop [command] Available Commands: check Run detectors over a file (or stdin) and emit a JSON report. completion Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell help Help about any command plainify Rewrite prose into plain English via `claude -p`. rewrite Rewrite a paragraph via `claude -p`, applying the slop-cop rewrite rules. rules Print the full rule catalogue as JSON. version Print build metadata as JSON. Flags: -h, --help help for slop-cop -v, --version version for slop-cop Use "slop-cop [command] --help" for more information about a command. AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md LICENSE NOTICE README.md bin cmd commands descriptor docs go.mod go.sum internal scripts skills # ![slop-cop](docs/assets/readme-banner.webp) **Never ship `delve` again.** slop-cop reads your agent's prose with 226 rules and returns a JSON rap sheet the agent revises against, in CI, pre-commit, or inline. [![CI](https://github.com/yasyf/slop-cop/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/yasyf/slop-cop/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/yasyf/slop-cop)](https://github.com/yasyf/slop-cop/releases/latest) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ## Get started ```bash brew install yasyf/tap/slop-cop slop-cop check draft.md --pretty ``` Driving with an agent? Paste this: ``` /plugin marketplace add yasyf/slop-cop /plugin install slop-cop@slop-cop ```
No plugin support? Paste this instead. ```text Install slop-cop with `brew install yasyf/tap/slop-cop`. Then run `slop-cop check README.md --pretty` and revise the file until the violations array is empty. ```
--- ## Use cases ### Make your agent self-edit before you ever see the draft You ask for a PR description and get "In today's fast-paced world" back, and then you spend the review playing copy editor. Install the plugin and its skill runs this loop on every draft, before the agent replies: ```bash printf '%s' "$draft" | slop-cop check --lang=markdown - ``` The agent walks the `violations` array, rewrites each `matchedText`, and re-checks until `counts_by_rule` is `{}`. You see the clean revision, never the slop. ### Catch the sentence nobody can parse, whoever typed it The slop layer polices prose that sounds like an LLM, and the new base layer underneath polices prose that is unclear. Its 9 plain-language rules flag the 45-word sentence, the padded `allows you to`, the passive that demotes its actor, and the paragraph carrying three ideas, in human prose and agent prose alike: ```bash slop-cop check docs/spec.md --standard=base ``` `--standard` picks the layer set. `all` is the default and runs every layer; `slop`, `base`, and `google` each run one layer alone. An unknown value exits `4`. ### Hold docs to the Google developer documentation style guide The google layer ports the [Google developer documentation style guide](https://developers.google.com/style) into 169 rules, and it is the standard the other layers defer to. It flags the title-case heading, the step you called `simply`, the `will` that describes constant behavior, the `click here` link, the passive that hides who acts, and the reader you addressed as "the user": ```bash slop-cop check docs/guide.md --standard=google ``` Every rule carries the guide section it came from, so `slop-cop rules --category=google` reads as an index into the guide. Where a Google rule and an older slop rule disagree, the Google rule wins the span it matched and the slop rule keeps firing everywhere else. `Run the following command:` stops tripping `colon-elaboration`, while `The result: chaos.` still does. ### Block era-openers and hedge stacks in CI and pre-commit Slop merges because nobody wants to be the reviewer who flags tone. Make the machine do it: ```bash slop-cop check docs/announcement.md --strict ``` `check` exits 0 whatever it finds and puts the verdict in the JSON; `--strict` turns a non-empty `violations` array into exit 1. The 178 client-side rules make no network calls, so the gate costs milliseconds. Test for the report's `ran` field before trusting an empty result. A run killed by a timeout leaves empty stdout, and without `--strict` its exit code matches a clean pass. If you gated CI on an earlier slop-only release, this gate now fails on base- and google-layer hits too. Pass `--standard=slop` to reproduce the old gate; its report is byte-identical to what earlier releases printed. 681 README.md 302 CHANGELOG.md 353 docs/guide.md 293 docs/de/anleitung.md 413 docs/fr/notes.md 272 docs/guides/setup.md 2314 total

Runs the 178 client-side rules by default. Two optional LLM passes
run via the codex CLI:

  low   sentence-tier semantic analysis, 40 rules
  high  low + document-tier structural analysis, 8 rules

Choose one with --llm-effort (off|low|high|auto), or use the sugar aliases:
  --llm       → --llm-effort=low
  --llm-deep  → --llm-effort=high
  --no-llm    → --llm-effort=off

$SLOP_COP_LLM takes the same four values and applies when no flag does.
When the codex CLI is on $PATH, --llm-effort=auto resolves to 'low';
otherwise 'off'. Auto-enabled passes fail open (the
failure is reported under 'llm.<tier>.error' and the client-side results
are still returned); explicit passes propagate the error as exit code 3.

Input is taken from the path argument, or from stdin when the path is "-"
or omitted.

Language-aware mode masks non-prose regions of the input before detectors
run, so slop-cop flags prose only — not code, tags, URLs, or other syntax.
Pick a mode with --lang:

  auto      (default) pick from the file extension; "text" for stdin.
  text      no masking; treat input as plain prose.
  markdown  CommonMark; mask code fences, links, HTML, YAML front matter.
  html      HTML; mask tags, attributes, <script>/<style>/<pre>/<code>.
  jsx,tsx   JS/TS with JSX; keep comments, strings, template quasis, JSX text.
  ts,js     JS/TS without JSX.

Suppressions inside masked modes drop structural false positives
(e.g. 'dramatic-fragment' on headings, 'staccato-burst' across list items).

The 226 rules come in three layers, all on by default. Pick with --standard:

  all     (default) every layer.
  slop    the original LLM-tell catalogue: does this sound like an LLM?
  base    the plain-language base layer: can this be read once and understood?
  google  the Google developer documentation style guide.

The selection applies to the LLM passes too — a layer left out never reaches
the prompt.

Individual rules are suppressed by a .slopcop.toml resolved by walking up from
the input path (--config overrides it):

  disable = ["colon-elaboration"]
  enable_only = ["overused-intensifiers"]

  [[overrides]]
  paths = ["docs/**/*.md"]
  disable = ["unformatted-code-identifier"]

Use --lines to report only the violations that begin within a 1-based inclusive
line range, while still scanning the whole document for context — useful for
linting just the lines an edit touched:

  50:80  a closed range          50:  from line 50 to EOF
  :80    from line 1 to line 80  50   a single line

Usage:
  slop-cop check [path|-] [flags]

Examples:
  slop-cop check article.md --pretty
  cat article.md | slop-cop check --no-llm
  slop-cop check component.tsx --lang=tsx --no-llm
  slop-cop check README.md --lines 50:80 --format=compact
  slop-cop check - --lang=markdown --llm-effort=high < article.md

Flags:
      --config string               Path to a .slopcop.toml. Default: the nearest one above the input path; its absence is not an error.
      --document-model string       Codex model slug for the document pass. (default "gpt-5.6-luna:low")
      --document-timeout duration   Wall-clock bound on the document pass, retries included. (default 3m0s)
      --format string               Output format: json (the full report) or compact (one tab-separated line per violation, then a counts line). (default "json")
  -h, --help                        help for check
      --lang string                 Input language: auto|text|markdown|html|jsx|tsx|ts|js. (default "auto")
      --lines string                Restrict the report to a 1-based inclusive line range, e.g. 50:80 (open-ended 50: or :80; a bare 50 is one line). Detectors still run over the full input.
      --llm                         Alias for --llm-effort=low (sentence tier).
      --llm-deep                    Alias for --llm-effort=high (sentence + document tiers).
      --llm-effort string           LLM analysis effort: off|low|high|auto. Auto = low when the codex CLI is on $PATH, off otherwise. $SLOP_COP_LLM sets it when no flag does. (default "auto")
      --no-llm                      Alias for --llm-effort=off (client-side rules only). Wins over --llm and --llm-deep.
      --pretty                      Indent JSON output.
      --sentence-model string       Codex model slug for the sentence pass. (default "gpt-5.6-luna:low")
      --sentence-timeout duration   Wall-clock bound on each sentence-pass chunk, retries included. (default 2m0s)
      --standard string             Rule layers to run: all (every layer), slop (the original LLM-tell catalogue), base (the plain-language base layer), google (the Google developer documentation style guide). (default "all")
      --strict                      Exit 1 when the report carries violations. Off by default: a completed run exits 0 whatever it found.

Runs the 178 client-side rules by default. Two optional LLM passes
run via the codex CLI:

  low   sentence-tier semantic analysis, 40 rules
  high  low + document-tier structural analysis, 8 rules

Choose one with --llm-effort (off|low|high|auto), or use the sugar aliases:
  --llm       → --llm-effort=low
  --llm-deep  → --llm-effort=high
  --no-llm    → --llm-effort=off

$SLOP_COP_LLM takes the same four values and applies when no flag does.
When the codex CLI is on $PATH, --llm-effort=auto resolves to 'low';
otherwise 'off'. Auto-enabled passes fail open (the
failure is reported under 'llm.<tier>.error' and the client-side results
are still returned); explicit passes propagate the error as exit code 3.

Input is taken from the path argument, or from stdin when the path is "-"
or omitted.

Language-aware mode masks non-prose regions of the input before detectors
run, so slop-cop flags prose only — not code, tags, URLs, or other syntax.
Pick a mode with --lang:

  auto      (default) pick from the file extension; "text" for stdin.
  text      no masking; treat input as plain prose.
  markdown  CommonMark; mask code fences, links, HTML, YAML front matter.
  html      HTML; mask tags, attributes, <script>/<style>/<pre>/<code>.
  jsx,tsx   JS/TS with JSX; keep comments, strings, template quasis, JSX text.
  ts,js     JS/TS without JSX.

Suppressions inside masked modes drop structural false positives
(e.g. 'dramatic-fragment' on headings, 'staccato-burst' across list items).

The 226 rules come in three layers, all on by default. Pick with --standard:

  all     (default) every layer.
  slop    the original LLM-tell catalogue: does this sound like an LLM?
  base    the plain-language base layer: can this be read once and understood?
  google  the Google developer documentation style guide.

The selection applies to the LLM passes too — a layer left out never reaches
the prompt.

Individual rules are suppressed by a .slopcop.toml resolved by walking up from
the input path (--config overrides it):

  enable_only = ["overused-intensifiers"]

  paths = ["docs/**/*.md"]
  disable = ["unformatted-code-identifier"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Benchmark wrapper: checker only. No model call, no network.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    rewrite|plainify) echo "slop-cop: $a is disabled in the benchmark (it calls the claude CLI); use check" >&2; exit 4 ;;
    --llm|--llm-deep|--llm-effort|--llm-effort=*) echo "slop-cop: model passes are disabled in the benchmark; use --no-llm" >&2; exit 4 ;;
  esac
done
export SLOP_COP_LLM=off
exec "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/slop-cop-real" "$@"

# slop-cop links tree-sitter (cgo), so every target must build with
# CGO_ENABLED=1 and a C toolchain. linux cross-compiles via `zig cc`
# (zig bundles a full cross C toolchain: static musl Linux);

    main: ./cmd/slop-cop
    binary: slop-cop
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=1
    goos:

    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }} -X main.commit={{ .Commit }}

        env:

          - "CC=zig cc -target x86_64-linux-musl"
          - "CXX=zig c++ -target x86_64-linux-musl"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fail if README.md or any Markdown file under docs/ reads like LLM output.
# Needs the slop-cop binary on PATH (brew install yasyf/tap/slop-cop).
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if ! command -v slop-cop >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "lint:prose: slop-cop not found on PATH (brew install yasyf/tap/slop-cop)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

status=0
while IFS= read -r file; do
  # --strict exits 1 on violations; any other non-zero code is a tool error.
  if ! report=$(slop-cop check "$file" --strict --no-llm --standard=slop --format=compact); then
    status=1
    echo "== $file" >&2
    echo "$report" >&2
  fi
done < <(find README.md docs -name '*.md' -type f | sort)

exit $status
EOF
